views.purpose: The code-mapping viewpoint is chosen because its type-level nodes and implements/located-in relations directly answer the questions about data entities, lifecycle persistence, extension points, and application dependencies within the persistence layer.
required_evidence: Mapping of data entities (users, reports, locations, categories, states, state changes, internal notes, notifications) to implementing types
Implementation structures showing persistence layer boundaries and extension points for future changes
Dependencies of application parts on the persisted information
views.diagram_language_rule: viewpoint agent chose plantuml: PlantUML can accurately depict the implementation mapping and relationships between architectural elements and their implementing types for AQ1, AQ2, AQ3, and AQ4.

notes: Eligible because they frame the chosen concerns: module-decomposition, code-mapping, decision-record

Module-decomposition was rejected because it focuses on coarse-grained modules and subsystems rather than the specific type-level mapping needed for data entities and lifecycle information, and decision-record was rejected because it documents architectural decisions rather than mapping the concrete data entities and their implementations.

diagram language plantuml: viewpoint agent chose plantuml: PlantUML can accurately depict the implementation mapping and relationships between architectural elements and their implementing types for AQ1, AQ2, AQ3, and AQ4.
